title: add-namespace-slice-and-ephemeral-init-claim-templates
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Private installs in large multi-tenant clusters were experiencing long init windows and occasional PV admission throttling when many tenant seed jobs ran concurrently. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: (1) namespaceSlices - a lightweight partitioning option that sequences tenant bootstrapping to reduce API pressure and (2) ephemeralInitClaims - a templated, short-lived PVC lifecycle for init jobs to avoid long-lived storage churn in airgapped and on-prem installs.

What changed: Added new top-level values schema keys `global.namespaceSlices` and `init.ephemeralClaimProfiles`. The chart templates now render an init-job helper that creates ephemeral PVCs with a short `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` (when supported by the CSI driver) or falls back to a deletion job. The namespace slicing feature injects a `slice` label onto tenant namespaces and the installer sequencer honors slice windows so only a configurable fraction of tenants run init concurrently. For airgapped installs the image pull templates now allow `preloadedImage` overrides with an explicit `imageManifestHash` check and a fail-open/close policy.

Upgrade/migration notes: This is backwards compatible by default. Existing installs will have namespaceSlices disabled and ephemeral profiles empty. To opt in, set `global.namespaceSlices.count > 1` and provide an `init.ephemeralClaimProfiles` entry. There is a migration helper `scripts/migrate-ephemeral-profiles.sh` included that annotates existing tenant namespaces with the chosen slice.

Checklist: 1) values schema added and validated; 2) templating for init job + PVC lifecycle; 3) e2e smoke in kind + onprem (gce-equivalent) with simulated CSI; 4) docs/upgrade note added.

Testing: Ran helm template/helm lint, unit tests for tpl helpers, an integration run in staging (10 tenants, slice=2) showed 52% reduction in simultaneous API server object create calls during install window. CI had an intermittent lint failure on a generated YAML indentation which was fixed in commit 3.

Risks & mitigation: If clusters have CSI drivers that do not support TTL or immediate deletion of PVCs we fallback to an explicit cleanup job that deletes bound PVCs and their backing volumes only when safe. The namespace slicing is opt-in and defaults to 1 (no slicing).
commits: add: values.schema.json additions for namespaceSlices and ephemeralClaimProfiles
feat:init templating: ephemeral pvc helper + delete-or-ttl cleanup job
fix: yaml lint and indentation in templates/init-job.yaml
review_comments: Elliot: Can we avoid needing CSI TTL by default? Suggest fallback delete-job pattern. Response: implemented fallback delete-job with safety checks (commit 2).
Kai: Are slices stable across upgrades? Response: slices are driven by annotation; migrate script added and documented (scripts/migrate-ephemeral-profiles.sh).
Rhea: Add E2E that simulates missing CSI TTL and verify cleanup. Response: added integration test manifest and run results attached in CI logs.
release_notes:
- Added namespace slicing (global.namespaceSlices) to sequence tenant init and reduce API pressure.
- Added ephemeral init PVC profiles (init.ephemeralClaimProfiles) with templated PVC lifecycle and cleanup fallback for non-TTL CSI drivers.
- Installer now supports preloadedImage overrides for airgapped setups with optional manifest hash verification.
files_snippet:
{{- define "redwood.ephemeralPVC" -}}
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: {{ .name }}-ephemeral
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: redwood-installer
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: {{ .size }}
  storageClassName: {{ .storageClass | default "local-fast" }}
{{- end -}}
notes_for_ops: Enable by setting global.namespaceSlices.count to a value >1 and configuring init.ephemeralClaimProfiles. For airgap installs set images.preloadedImage (with optional imageManifestHash) and ensure the installer has access to the image registry mirror. The migrate script will annotate existing namespaces; run it with --dry-run first.
